title.en: to be: I am, you are · subject pronouns

summary.es: to be: I am, you are · subject pronouns

explanation.es:
El verbo to be: I am, you are

En inglés be significa a la vez ser y estar. En presente tiene tres formas: am, is y are. Hoy empezamos con dos:

Forma completaContracciónSignificado
I am Ana.I'm Ana.Soy Ana.
You are Tom.You're Tom.Eres Tom.
I am fine.I'm fine.Estoy bien.
En la conversación se usan casi siempre las contracciones: I'm, you're. I (yo) se escribe siempre con mayúscula.

Saludos y despedidas

EnglishCuándo
Hello! / Hi!a cualquier hora (hi es más informal)
Good morningpor la mañana
Good afternoondespués de las 12
Good eveningpor la tarde-noche, al llegar
Good nightsolo para despedirse o al ir a dormir
Goodbye! / Bye!al irse
— Hello! I'm Lucy. What's your name?
— Hi, Lucy! I'm Ken. Nice to meet you.
— Nice to meet you too.

Ojo

Errores típicos de hispanohablantes:
  • ✗ I Ana. → ✓ I'm Ana. (el verbo no se puede omitir)
  • ✗ Good night (al llegar a las 21:00) → ✓ Good evening
  • ✗ My name is is Pedro → ✓ My name is Pedro / I'm Pedro

examples.en: I am Lucy.
You are my friend.
Good night ! I'm going to bed.
examples.es: ¡Buenas noches! Me voy a la cama.

examples.en: Nice to meet you.
What's your name?
I'm Pedro.

title.en: to be: he is, she is, it is, we are, they are · Where…from?

summary.es: to be: he is, she is, it is, we are, they are · Where…from?

explanation.es:
Todas las formas de to be en presente

AfirmativaContracciónSignificado
I amI'myo soy/estoy
you areyou'retú eres / usted es
he / she / it ishe's / she's / it'sél / ella es; ello es
we arewe'renosotros somos
you areyou'revosotros sois / ustedes son
they arethey'reellos / ellas son
It se usa para cosas, animales y lugares (no existe en español): It's a big city = Es una ciudad grande. You vale para tú, usted, vosotros y ustedes.

Preguntar el origen

En las preguntas el verbo va antes del sujeto. La preposición from suele ir al final:

Where are you from? — I'm from Spain. I'm Spanish.
Where is she from? — She's from Japan. She's Japanese.
Where are they from? — They're from China. They're Chinese.
Países, nacionalidades e idiomas se escriben con mayúscula: Spain, Spanish, Japan, Japanese, China, Chinese.
Errores típicos:
  • ✗ Is from Madrid. → ✓ He's from Madrid. (el sujeto es obligatorio)
  • ✗ I'm spanish. → ✓ I'm Spanish.
  • ✗ From where are you? → ✓ Where are you from?

examples.en: She is from Japan.
We are from Spain.
Where are they from?
Madrid is a big city .
Where are you from?
They are from a small town.

title.en: to be: negative and questions · question words: what, how old, who · numbers 1–100

summary.es: to be: negative and questions · question words: what, how old, who · numbers 1–100

explanation.es:
Negativa y preguntas con to be

NegativaPreguntaRespuesta corta
I'm not 20.Am I late?Yes, you are. / No, you aren't.
You aren't married.Are you a student?Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.
She isn't here.Is she your sister?Yes, she is. / No, she isn't.
They aren't from Peru.Are they English?Yes, they are. / No, they aren't.
Las respuestas cortas repiten el verbo: Yes, I am. (no solo «Yes»). En la respuesta afirmativa no se contrae: ✗ Yes, I'm.

La edad: be, no have

How old are you? — I'm 25. / I'm 25 years old.
✗ I have 25 years. → ✓ I'm 25. En inglés la edad se expresa con be.

Palabras interrogativas

What's your phone number?¿Cuál es tu número de teléfono?
What's your address?¿Cuál es tu dirección?
Who's that?¿Quién es ese?
How do you spell it?¿Cómo se escribe?
Números: thirteen (13) y thirty (30) suenan parecido; en -teen el acento va al final (thirTEEN) y en -ty al principio (THIRty). Del 21 al 99 se escribe con guion: twenty-one, forty-five.

examples.en: I am 30 years old.
She isn't married. She's single.
Are you a student?
How old is your brother?
What's your phone number?
How do you spell your last name?

title.en: a / an · plural nouns · this, that, these, those

summary.es: a / an · plural nouns · this, that, these, those

explanation.es:
a / an

Delante de un sustantivo singular contable necesitas a o an (un/una). Depende del sonido, no de la letra:

a + sonido consonantean + sonido vocal
a book, a pen, auniversity (/ju/)an apple, an umbrella, anhour (h muda)

Plurales

ReglaEjemplo
+ sbook → books, key → keys
-s, -sh, -ch, -x + esbox → boxes, watch → watches
consonante + y → iesdictionary → dictionaries
irregularesman → men, woman → women, child → children, person → people
Los adjetivos no tienen plural: two big boxes (✗ bigs).

this · that · these · those

cercalejos
singularthis penthat door
pluralthese pensthose doors
What's this? — It's an umbrella.
What are those? — They're my glasses.
✗ It's umbrella. → ✓ It's an umbrella. · ✗ This are my keys. → ✓ These are my keys.

examples.en: It's an umbrella.
It's a dictionary.
These are my keys.
There are three boxes on the table.
examples.es: Hay tres cajas en la mesa.

examples.en: What's that on the desk?
examples.es: ¿Qué es eso que hay en el escritorio?

examples.en: These are my new pencils.

title.en: possessive adjectives: my, your, his, her… · possessive 's · whose

summary.es: possessive adjectives: my, your, his, her… · possessive 's · whose

explanation.es:
Adjetivos posesivos

SujetoPosesivoEjemplo
Imymy mother
youyouryour brother
hehishis wife
sheherher husband
ititsits name
weourour parents
theytheirtheir children
His / her dependen del poseedor, no de la cosa: Tom and his sister, Ana and her brother. En español «su» vale para todos; en inglés hay que elegir. Los posesivos no cambian en plural: my parents.

El genitivo sajón: 's

Para decir «el/la … de una persona», el poseedor va primero + 's:

Maria's brother = el hermano de María
my parents' house = la casa de mis padres
the children's toys = los juguetes de los niños
Whose = ¿de quién? — Whose bag is this? — It's Tom's.
✗ the brother of Maria → ✓ Maria's brother · ✗ Ana and his father → ✓ Ana and her father · ✗ Who's bag? → ✓ Whose bag?

examples.en: Laura and her husband live in London.
examples.es: Laura y su marido viven en Londres.

examples.en: Peter loves his daughter.
examples.es: Peter quiere mucho a su hija.

examples.en: This is my parents' car. (my parents)
examples.es: Este es el coche de mis padres.

examples.en: Whose phone is this? — It's Anna's.
examples.es: ¿De quién es este móvil? — Es de Anna.

examples.en: My sister's husband is a doctor.
examples.es: El marido de mi hermana es médico.

examples.en: Their children are very young.

title.en: have got / has got · adjectives: position · very, quite

summary.es: have got / has got · adjectives: position · very, quite

explanation.es:
have got

Have got significa «tener» (posesión, aspecto, familia). Es muy británico y casi siempre va contraído:

AfirmativaNegativaPregunta
I've got blue eyes.I haven't got a car.Have you got a pen?
She's got long hair.He hasn't got a beard.Has she got children?
Respuestas cortas: Yes, I have. / No, she hasn't. (sin got). En inglés americano se dice más I have / Do you have…? Las dos formas son correctas.
She's got = she has got (no «is»). ✗ She have got → ✓ She has got.

Los adjetivos: antes del sustantivo e invariables

a tall man · long black hair · blue eyes · She's very pretty. · He's quite shy.
Al revés que en español: ✗ hair black → ✓ black hair. Nunca llevan -s: ✗ blues eyes. Opinión antes que descripción: a nice young man.
hair (pelo de la cabeza) es incontable: ✗ She's got long hairs. → ✓ long hair.

examples.en: She 's got green eyes.
Have you got a brother?
My dad hasn't got a beard.
He's got short brown hair.
examples.es: Tiene el pelo corto y castaño.

examples.en: My brother is tall and very funny.
examples.es: Mi hermano es alto y muy gracioso.

examples.en: Have you got a big family?

title.en: present simple: I / you / we / they · do / don't · a / an + job

summary.es: present simple: I / you / we / they · do / don't · a / an + job

explanation.es:
Presente simple: hábitos y hechos

Con I, you, we, they el verbo no cambia. Para negar y preguntar usamos el auxiliar do:

AfirmativaNegativaPregunta
I work in a bank.I don't work at weekends.Do you work here?
They speak English.We don't speak French.Where do they live?
don't = do not. Respuestas cortas: Yes, I do. / No, I don't. La pregunta típica sobre el trabajo es What do you do? (= ¿a qué te dedicas?).

Profesiones con a / an

I'm a teacher. · She's an engineer. · He works in a hospital. · They work for a big company.
✗ I'm teacher. → ✓ I'm a teacher. (en español no hay artículo, en inglés es obligatorio) · ✗ I not work. → ✓ I don't work. · ✗ You work here? → ✓ Do you work here?

examples.en: I'm an engineer.
We don't work on Sundays.
Do you like your job?
Nurses work in a hospital .
examples.es: Los enfermeros trabajan en un hospital.

examples.en: Where do you work?
They don't need a car for their job.
examples.es: No necesitan coche para su trabajo.

title.en: present simple: he / she / it (-s) · does / doesn't · telling the time

summary.es: present simple: he / she / it (-s) · does / doesn't · telling the time

explanation.es:
He / she / it: el verbo lleva -s

AfirmativaNegativaPregunta
She works.She doesn't work.Does she work?
He gets up at 7.He doesn't get up early.What time does he get up?
Con does / doesn't el verbo pierde la -s: ✗ Does she works? → ✓ Does she work?

Ortografía de la -s

la mayoría + sworks, reads, sleeps
-s, -sh, -ch, -x, -o + eswatches, washes, goes, does
consonante + y → iesstudy → studies
irregularhave → has

La hora

7:00seven o'clock
7:15quarter past seven
7:30half past seven
7:45quarter to eight
7:20twenty past seven / seven twenty
What time is it? — It's half past eight.
She has breakfast at eight and goes to work at nine.
El error más frecuente en todos los niveles: olvidar la -s. ✗ She work in a shop. → ✓ She works. · «a las» = at: at 7 o'clock. · «tener el desayuno» = have breakfast (✗ take breakfast).

examples.en: My mother gets up at six.
examples.es: Mi madre se levanta a las seis.

examples.en: He watches TV in the evening.
examples.es: Ve la tele por la tarde.

examples.en: Does she have lunch at home?
Tom doesn't work on Fridays.
She has a shower every morning.
What time does the film start?

title.en: adverbs of frequency: always, usually, often, sometimes, never · like / love / hate + -ing · How often…?

summary.es: adverbs of frequency: always, usually, often, sometimes, never · like / love / hate + -ing · How often…?

explanation.es:
Adverbios de frecuencia

always100%siempre
usually80%normalmente
often60%a menudo
sometimes40%a veces
hardly ever5%casi nunca
never0%nunca

Posición: antes del verbo principal, pero después de be:

I often play tennis. · She never watches TV. · He's always late.
never ya es negativo: ✗ I don't never… → ✓ I never go. Para expresiones como every day, once a week, twice a month: al final de la frase. Pregunta: How often do you…?

like / love / hate + -ing

I love dancing. · She doesn't like swimming. · They hate shopping. · Do you enjoy reading?
Ortografía de -ing: dance → dancing (se va la e), swim → swimming, shop → shopping (se dobla la consonante). enjoy siempre con -ing.
«Me gusta el fútbol» = I like football (sin «the», y el sujeto es I). ✗ Like me football. ✗ I like the football.

examples.en: I often go to the cinema on Fridays.
examples.es: A menudo voy al cine los viernes.

examples.en: She is always tired after work.
examples.es: Siempre está cansada después del trabajo.

examples.en: He loves swimming .
How often do you play tennis?
We usually play football at the weekend.
examples.es: Normalmente jugamos al fútbol el fin de semana.

examples.en: I go swimming once a week.
examples.es: Voy a nadar una vez a la semana.

title.en: prepositions of time: at, on, in · ordinal numbers · dates

summary.es: prepositions of time: at, on, in · ordinal numbers · dates

explanation.es:
at · on · in

UsoEjemplos
athoras y momentos concretosat 6 o'clock, at night, at the weekend, at Christmas
ondías y fechason Monday, on 5th May, on my birthday, on Friday night
inmeses, estaciones, años y partes del díain May, in summer, in 2025, in the morning
Sin preposición: today, tomorrow, yesterday, this week, next year, every day. ✗ on next Monday → ✓ next Monday. Truco: at = punto, on = día, in = periodo largo.

Ordinales y fechas

1st first · 2nd second · 3rd third · 4th fourth · 5th fifth · 12th twelfth · 20th twentieth · 21st twenty-first

Se escribe 5 May o 5th May, pero se dice the fifth of May (RU) o May fifth (EE. UU.). Días y meses siempre con mayúscula.

When's your birthday? — It's on the 3rd of March.
✗ in Monday → ✓ on Monday · ✗ in the night → ✓ at night · ✗ monday, april → ✓ Monday, April

examples.en: My birthday is in June.
The party is on Saturday.
I go to bed at eleven o'clock.
We go to the beach in summer.
examples.es: Vamos a la playa en verano.

examples.en: When is your birthday?
I don't work at the weekend.
examples.es: No trabajo el fin de semana.

title.en: countable and uncountable nouns · some / any · How much…? / How many…?

summary.es: countable and uncountable nouns · some / any · How much…? / How many…?

explanation.es:
Contables e incontables

Contables (se pueden contar)Incontables (no se cuentan)
an apple, two apples, an egg, three potatoeswater, milk, bread, rice, cheese, sugar, meat
tienen plural y van con a / ansin plural ni a / an
Para contar incontables usamos envases o unidades: a bottle of water, a cup of coffee, a slice of bread, a kilo of rice.

some / any

somefrases afirmativasThere's some milk. I've got some eggs.
anynegativas y preguntasWe haven't got any bread. Are there any apples?
some en ofrecimientos y peticionesWould you like some tea? Can I have some water?

How much? · How many?

How many eggs do we need? (contables)
How much sugar do you want? (incontables)
How much is it? — It's £3. (precio)
✗ a bread → ✓ some bread / a loaf of bread · ✗ breads, informations → ✓ bread, information · ✗ How much apples? → ✓ How many apples?

examples.en: There isn't any milk in the fridge.
examples.es: No hay leche en la nevera.

examples.en: I'd like some water, please.
How many apples do you want?
How much rice do we need?
Are there any eggs in the kitchen?
I have a cup of tea every morning.
examples.es: Me tomo una taza de té todas las mañanas.

title.en: there is / there are · prepositions of place: in, on, under, next to, between, behind, in front of

summary.es: there is / there are · prepositions of place: in, on, under, next to, between, behind, in front of

explanation.es:
there is / there are

Equivale a «hay». Se elige según lo que viene después:

Singular / incontablePlural
+There's a sofa. There's some milk.There are two bedrooms.
−There isn't a garden.There aren't any chairs.
?Is there a shower? — Yes, there is.Are there any shops? — No, there aren't.
✗ Has a garden. / ✗ There is two rooms. → ✓ There are two rooms. «Hay» no es have: My flat has two rooms (mi piso tiene) pero There are two rooms (hay).

Preposiciones de lugar

in the boxdentro deon the tableencima de (tocando)
under the beddebajo debehind the doordetrás de
next to the windowal lado debetween A and Bentre
in front of the housedelante denear the stationcerca de
There's a lamp next to the sofa. The keys are on the shelf. Is there a cat under the bed?
Ojo: in front of = delante de; opposite = enfrente de (al otro lado).

examples.en: There are two bathrooms in my house.
examples.es: Hay dos baños en mi casa.

examples.en: Is there a garden?
The cat is under the bed.
examples.es: El gato está debajo de la cama.

examples.en: The lamp is next to the sofa.
examples.es: La lámpara está al lado del sofá.

examples.en: There's a big window in the living room.
examples.es: Hay una ventana grande en el salón.

examples.en: My books are on the shelf behind the door.
examples.es: Mis libros están en la estantería detrás de la puerta.

title.en: imperative: Turn left. Don't cross. · Excuse me, where's…? · Let's…

summary.es: imperative: Turn left. Don't cross. · Excuse me, where's…? · Let's…

explanation.es:
El imperativo

Es la forma base del verbo, sin sujeto. Sirve para instrucciones, indicaciones y consejos:

AfirmativoNegativo
Turn left.Don't turn right.
Go straight on.Don't cross here.
Be careful!Don't be late!
Para sugerir algo que hacemos juntos: Let's + verbo: Let's take a taxi. Para sonar educado añade please: Sit down, please.

Pedir y dar indicaciones

— Excuse me, where's the station?
— Go straight on and take the second street on the left. It's on the corner, opposite the bank.
— Is it far? — No, it's about five minutes' walk.
turn left / rightgirar a la izquierda / derecha
go straight onseguir recto
cross the streetcruzar la calle
on the corneren la esquina
Excuse me = para llamar la atención o pedir paso; Sorry = para disculparte. ✗ No turn left → ✓ Don't turn left.

examples.en: Turn left at the bank.
examples.es: Gira a la izquierda en el banco.

examples.en: Don't cross the street here! It's dangerous.
examples.es: ¡No cruces la calle aquí! Es peligroso.

examples.en: Excuse me, where's the museum?
Let's go to the park. It's sunny!
Take the second street on the right.
examples.es: Toma la segunda calle a la derecha.

examples.en: Is there a supermarket near here?

title.en: can / can't (ability, permission, requests) · well, very well, not at all

summary.es: can / can't (ability, permission, requests) · well, very well, not at all

explanation.es:
can / can't

Can expresa habilidad (saber hacer), posibilidad y permiso. Es igual para todas las personas y va seguido del verbo sin to:

AfirmativaNegativaPregunta
I can swim.I can't drive.Can you cook?
She can speak French.He can't sing.Can she play the piano?
Nunca: ✗ She cans, ✗ can to swim, ✗ Do you can? Respuestas cortas: Yes, I can. / No, I can't.can't = cannot (una sola palabra).

Pedir y dar permiso

Can I open the window? — Yes, of course. / Sorry, you can't.
Can you help me, please? — Sure!

¿Qué tal lo haces?

I can swim very well. · He can cook quite well. · I can't dance at all.
tocar un instrumento = play the guitar / piano; saber nadar = can swim (no know swim).

examples.en: My grandmother can't use a computer.
examples.es: Mi abuela no sabe usar un ordenador.

examples.en: Can you ride a horse?
She can speak three languages.
I play the guitar in a band.
examples.es: Toco la guitarra en un grupo.

examples.en: I can't dance at all.
Can you help me with this box?

title.en: present continuous: am / is / are + -ing · now, at the moment

summary.es: present continuous: am / is / are + -ing · now, at the moment

explanation.es:
Presente continuo

am / is / are + verbo-ing. Expresa algo que está pasando ahora, en este momento:

AfirmativaNegativaPregunta
I'm reading.I'm not sleeping.Are you listening?
She's talking on the phone.It isn't raining.What is he doing?
They're waiting.We aren't working.Why are they laughing?

Ortografía de -ing

casi todos + ingread → reading, play → playing
-e: quita la ewrite → writing, smile → smiling
vocal + consonante final: doblasit → sitting, run → running, swim → swimming
-ie → yinglie → lying
Señales: now, right now, at the moment, Look!, Listen! El español usa el presente simple muchas veces donde el inglés exige el continuo: «¿Qué haces?» (ahora) = What are you doing?
✗ She reading. → ✓ She's reading. · ✗ What do you do now? → ✓ What are you doing now?

examples.en: Be quiet! The baby is sleeping.
Look! It's snowing .
What are you doing?
They're sitting on the sofa.
Why are you laughing?
She's talking on the phone right now.
examples.es: Ahora mismo está hablando por teléfono.

title.en: object pronouns: me, you, him, her, it, us, them · How much is / are…? · one / ones

summary.es: object pronouns: me, you, him, her, it, us, them · How much is / are…? · one / ones

explanation.es:
Pronombres de objeto

SujetoObjetoEjemplo
ImeCan you help me?
youyouI love you.
he / she / ithim / her / itI like her dress. I like it.
weusCome with us.
theythemThese shoes? I'll take them.
Van después del verbo o de la preposición (al revés que en español): I see her every day (la veo). for me, with him, to them.

En la tienda

— Can I help you?
— Yes, how much is this jacket? / How much are these jeans?
— It's £45. / They're £30.
— Can I try it on? Have you got it in a bigger size?
— Sure. Do you want the black one or the blue one?
— The blue one, please. Can I pay by credit card?
trousers, jeans, glasses son plurales: These jeans are… I like them. ✗ a trouser · one / ones evita repetir: the red one, the cheap ones.

examples.en: Where's Anna? I can't see her .
These shoes are nice. How much are they?
This dress is too big. Have you got a smaller one ?
examples.es: Este vestido es demasiado grande. ¿Tiene uno más pequeño?

examples.en: Can I pay by credit card?
Can I try it on, please?
I like the red one but it's expensive.
examples.es: Me gusta el rojo, pero es caro.

title.en: present simple vs present continuous · It's sunny / It's raining · What's the weather like?

summary.es: present simple vs present continuous · It's sunny / It's raining · What's the weather like?

explanation.es:
El tiempo

Con el tiempo siempre usamos el sujeto it:

It's sunny / cloudy / windy / foggy.Hace sol / Está nublado / Hace viento / Hay niebla.
It's hot / warm / cool / cold.Hace calor / buen tiempo / fresco / frío.
It's raining / snowing.Está lloviendo / nevando (ahora).
What's the weather like today? — It's cold and it's raining.

Presente simple o continuo

Presente simplePresente continuo
hábitos, cosas generales y permanenteslo que pasa ahora o estos días
It rains a lot in London.It's raining now.
I usually wear jeans.Today I'm wearing a dress.
usually, often, every day, in winternow, at the moment, today, this week
Algunos verbos casi nunca van en continuo porque expresan estados: like, love, want, need, know, understand, believe. ✗ I'm knowing → ✓ I know.
✗ Is raining. / ✗ Makes cold. → ✓ It's raining. / ✓ It's cold. (en español «hace frío», en inglés it is cold)

examples.en: It's very cold today.
It often rains in April.
Take an umbrella. It 's raining now.
What's the weather like in summer?
What's the weather like in Tokyo?
It's sunny but it's quite cold.

title.en: past of be: was / were · there was / there were · yesterday, last…, ago

summary.es: past of be: was / were · there was / there were · yesterday, last…, ago

explanation.es:
was / were

AfirmativaNegativaPregunta
I / he / she / it waswasn'tWas he at home?
you / we / they wereweren'tWere you tired?
I was at home yesterday. · We were at the beach last week.
Were you at the party? — Yes, I was. / No, I wasn't.
There was a concert. There were a lot of people.
Expresiones de pasado: yesterday, last night, last week, last year, two days ago, in 2010. ¡Sin preposición delante de last! ✗ the last week (cuando significa «la semana pasada»).

Nacer: be born

I was born in 1998. Where were you born?
✗ I born in Madrid. → ✓ I was born in Madrid. · «hace dos años» = two years ago (al final).

examples.en: I was very tired yesterday.
Were you at home last night?
There were many people at the concert.
examples.es: Había mucha gente en el concierto.

examples.en: She was born in Japan twenty years ago .
examples.es: Nació en Japón hace veinte años.

examples.en: Where were you last weekend?
examples.es: ¿Dónde estuviste el fin de semana pasado?

examples.en: The film wasn't very good.
examples.es: La película no era muy buena.

title.en: past simple: regular (-ed) and irregular verbs · did / didn't · What did you do?

summary.es: past simple: regular (-ed) and irregular verbs · did / didn't · What did you do?

explanation.es:
Pasado simple: verbos regulares

Añadimos -ed. La forma es igual para todas las personas:

work → workedlive → livedstudy → studiedstop → stopped

Verbos irregulares (¡a memorizar!)

go → wenthave → hadsee → saweat → ate
buy → boughtmake → mademeet → metget → got
come → cametake → tookdo → diddrink → drank

Negativa y preguntas con did

NegativaPregunta
I didn't go out.Did you go out?
She didn't like the film.What did you do last weekend?
Con did / didn't el verbo vuelve a la forma base: ✗ Did you went? → ✓ Did you go? ✗ I didn't saw → ✓ I didn't see.
Last Saturday I visited my grandparents. We had lunch together and then we watched a film. I didn't go out in the evening.
Pronunciación de -ed: /t/ worked, /d/ played, /ɪd/ solo tras t o d: wanted, visited. ✗ work-ED.

examples.en: Yesterday I went to the cinema.
We had dinner at a nice restaurant.
Did you see the match last night?
She didn't like the film.
I met my friends in the park.
examples.es: Quedé con mis amigos en el parque.

examples.en: They didn't come to the party.

title.en: be going to + verb · would like / I'd like · want to

summary.es: be going to + verb · would like / I'd like · want to

explanation.es:
be going to

Para planes e intenciones ya decididos: am / is / are + going to + verbo.

AfirmativaNegativaPregunta
I'm going to visit Rome.I'm not going to stay at home.Are you going to travel?
She's going to learn Japanese.They aren't going to come.What are you going to do tomorrow?
Muy parecido al español «voy a + infinitivo», ¡pero no olvides el verbo be! ✗ I going to → ✓ I'm going to.

would like · want

I'd like a coffee, please.Querría / Me gustaría un café.
I'd like to visit Japan one day.Me gustaría visitar Japón algún día.
Would you like to come?¿Te gustaría venir?
I want to go home.Quiero irme a casa.
I'd like es más educado que I want para pedir algo en una tienda o restaurante. Would you like…? = ofrecer/invitar; Do you like…? = preguntar por gustos.

examples.en: We're going to visit my aunt tomorrow.
examples.es: Mañana vamos a visitar a mi tía.

examples.en: Are you going to travel this summer?
I'd like a glass of water, please.
examples.es: Quería un vaso de agua, por favor.

examples.en: Would you like to come to the party?
What are you going to do tonight?
I'd like to live abroad one day.
examples.es: Me gustaría vivir en el extranjero algún día.
